clue.text: Very keen on Prague centre's own goal

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the letters at its heart are kept

blocks.note: the two middle letters of the six-letter city name
OG is the standard abbreviation for own goal in football reports

explanation.surface: A fan in Prague's stadium is thrilled by an own goal in the city centre.
explanation.walkthrough: PRAGUE has six letters, so its centre is a pair: the third and fourth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone agog is eagerly excited and impatient to see or hear something, so very keen.

clue.text: Take control of evacuated remote pub harbouring insurgent leader

indicators.note: emptied out means the inside is removed, leaving only the outer letters
a harbour shelters ships within it, so one piece sits inside another
the leader comes first, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: first and last letters once the middle is emptied
an inn is a pub
the first letter

explanation.surface: Authorities take back a remote pub that has been sheltering a rebel commander.
explanation.walkthrough: The insurgent's initial goes between the two Ns of INN, and the shell of REMOTE comes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in a horse is to pull the reins and restrain it, so figuratively to take control of something.

clue.text: Answer odd R&D queries when needed

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: A is the usual abbreviation for answer
the letters of R, D and the word queries

explanation.surface: A lab team handles strange research-and-development queries only when necessary.
explanation.walkthrough: The ampersand is dropped and R and D join the fodder as plain letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something as required means doing it at the point the situation calls for it, i.e. whenever necessary.

clue.text: Oversensitive youth, nervous about college

indicators.note: a nervous thing is jittery and agitated, so its letters are shaken into a new order
about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: taken as written
C is a common abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A thin-skinned teenager is anxious about going to college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nervous' reads as describing the youth, but it is the signal to rearrange; C for college is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchy person takes offence easily, which is exactly being oversensitive.

clue.text: Remove cream to guzzle without partner's being mean

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: to skim milk is to take the cream off it
to pig is to eat greedily
in bridge, North and South are partners, so one partner is N

explanation.surface: Someone stingy skims the cream and guzzles alone, refusing to share with their partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'lacking', but here it means outside: PIG goes round N. Bridge players sit as North, South, East and West, in partnerships.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimping is spending or using as little as possible, so being stingy or mean with money or effort.

clue.text: Artist's picture heartily upset Russian leader

indicators.note: from the heart, so only the central letter is taken
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: RA, a Royal Academician, plus the S of the possessive
the middle letter of the seven

explanation.surface: An artist's portrait of a Russian ruler has been knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is the usual crossword artist; the 's supplies an S.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor who ruled Russia before the 1917 revolution, so its leader.

clue.text: Off-road vehicle has decibels I tremble to describe

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw a line round it, so one piece encircles another

blocks.note: to quake is to tremble
dB is the symbol for decibels
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noisy off-roader is so loud that the rider shakes describing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describe' seems to mean putting into words; in crosswords it means drawing round, as a circle is described around a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A quad bike is a four-wheeled motorbike built for rough terrain, a classic off-road vehicle.

clue.text: Crop broadcast for web

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard rather than read, so the sound of a word matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: maize is a cereal crop, corn

explanation.surface: Farm produce is promoted on air for an online audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' could mean sowing seed, which suits the crop, but here it signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A web is a tangled network, and a maze is a confusing network of paths, so the two overlap figuratively.

clue.text: Government uses spin taking on Labour theory

indicators.note: to spin something is to turn it round, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for government
taken as written
labour is work

explanation.surface: A political spin doctor adopts a Labour Party policy idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour with a capital L looks like the political party; it is plain labour, meaning toil.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory not yet proved is conjecture, and guesswork is reasoning based on conjecture.

clue.text: Spa facility gets top rating in tabloid article

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
A is the top grade
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A health spa wins a five-star review in a tabloid feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The top grade sits inside the paper's name, and the article follows on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a hot steam room, one of the standard facilities offered at a spa.

clue.text: Information on category

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.walkthrough: Both short words here give letters; neither is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a kind or type of artistic work, such as a thriller, so a category.

clue.text: Nearly attended game with City

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: came, short of its final letter
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone almost went to a match against a city team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attended' in the sense of came along to an event; 'City' looks like a football club but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is an English university city, an example of the class named by the definition.

clue.text: A hundred break truce over New Year

indicators.note: to break something is to shatter its form, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A hundred combatants violate the ceasefire over the New Year holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Year' looks like a festival but supplies two abbreviations that join the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A century is a set of one hundred, whether years or runs scored in cricket.

clue.text: Look after church director

indicators.note: after means following, so the first piece named is placed second

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
an air is a look or manner

explanation.surface: A parish leader is asked to take care of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as one phrasal verb meaning care for; split it, and 'after' is only a positional signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The chair of a meeting or board is the person who presides over it, a director of proceedings.

clue.text: Cool French detective's taking time to visit

blocks.note: in means fashionable, cool
flic is French slang for a police officer
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A stylish French sleuth takes a while to drop in on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visit' looks like calling on someone, but it is the old sense of imposing a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To visit a plague or penalty upon people is to impose it, which is what inflict means.

clue.text: Just developing a style for children's stories

indicators.note: something developing is changing shape, so the letters are being rearranged

blocks.note: just means fair
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer is only now finding a voice suited to children's books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like an adverb meaning merely; it is the adjective meaning equitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy tales are traditional magical narratives told to young readers, a type of tale for kids.

clue.text: Worn-out old reservists getting dry and cosy at last

indicators.note: at last points to the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol
its final letter

explanation.surface: Exhausted veteran soldiers finally get warm and dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' fits because the TA was renamed the Army Reserve in 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty describes things shabby and worn through long use, the same sense as worn-out.

clue.text: Repaired marble, cutting line for resin

indicators.note: a repaired object has been put back together, so the letters are reassembled
cutting something out removes it, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: the word with its L cut out
L is the abbreviation for line, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A restorer fixes a marble statue, removing a line of resin filler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' could suggest insertion; here it means the line is cut out of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is fossilised tree resin, prized as a gemstone, so a specific kind of resin.

clue.text: Public transport head acquiring international company

indicators.note: to acquire is to take something in, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: a bus is public transport
I is the abbreviation for international
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: The boss of a transport firm buys a multinational corporation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a chief executive; it is a geographical headland, as in place names like Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: A business is a commercial firm, and company is a direct synonym for such an enterprise.

clue.text: On-line fixer found among stereotype geeks

indicators.note: found among says the letters are lying inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Internet troubleshooters are stereotyped as geeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On-line' looks like internet; it means on the washing line.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes peg pins washing to a clothes line, so it is something that fixes items on a line.

clue.text: Pincer movement caught thief heading for shopping mall

indicators.note: movement means shifting position, so the letters move about
a heading is at the top, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
first letter

explanation.surface: Police in a pincer movement catch a thief heading for the mall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pincer movement' reads as a military or police tactic, but it splits into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopping precinct is a British pedestrianised area of shops, much like an open-air shopping mall.

clue.text: Writer rejected investing in computers as foolish

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters run the other way
to invest in is to put something into, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a pen is a writer, something to write with
IT, information technology, means computers

explanation.surface: An author turned down a tech investment as unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like an author; in crosswords it is often the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or lacking sense, and foolish behaviour is a fair synonym in that sense.

clue.text: What's left of engineers' team bringing in union

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so one piece is put within another

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a side is a team
U is the abbreviation for union

explanation.surface: The remains of an engineers' works team after it joins a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in engineers' only smooths the surface; the possessive gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is the remainder after the main part has gone, a noun meaning whatever remains.

clue.text: Old ally worried, seeing limits of Tory fidelity

indicators.note: a worried thing is agitated and churned up, so the letters are mixed
limits are the edges, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A long-standing partner is anxious about how far Conservative faithfulness goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidelity is faithfulness to a person or cause, which is what loyalty means.

clue.text: Student's jog spoiled by morning congestion

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate
taken as written
am, ante meridiem, means morning

explanation.surface: A student's morning run is ruined by rush-hour traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Student just makes the surface possessive and adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A logjam is a blockage of floating timber, and figuratively any jam or deadlock, so congestion.

clue.text: Picked up inflatable mattress to go into hiding

indicators.note: picked up as a signal or rumour is heard, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: a Lilo is a British brand of inflatable airbed, used on beaches and for camping

explanation.surface: Someone grabs an airbed in order to hide away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' could mean physically lifting the mattress; it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is to keep out of sight and avoid attention, the idiom for hiding away.

clue.text: Disappearing with commercial vehicle is nigh hopeless

indicators.note: hopeless means a mess, beyond rescue, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a van is a commercial vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A disappearing delivery van means the situation is close to desperate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopeless' looks like the surface's verdict on the situation; it tells you to rearrange the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanishing means passing out of sight, so the present participle of disappear is an exact synonym.

clue.text: Video Assistant Referee has ultimate authority to make a change

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so only the final letter is taken

blocks.note: VAR is football's video review system
its last letter

explanation.surface: The video referee has the final say over whether a decision is overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimate authority' sounds like supreme power; split it, and it is just the last letter of authority.
explanation.definitionFit: To vary is to alter or differ, so the verb means to bring about a change.

clue.text: Elite forces given hard-to-get belt

blocks.note: the SAS, Special Air Service, is the British army's elite special forces regiment
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils; the rest only decorates the surface

explanation.surface: Special forces soldiers are awarded a rare decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the hard of 'hard-to-get' supplies a letter; the hyphenated phrase hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of fabric worn round the waist or over the shoulder, a kind of belt.

clue.text: Field in biplane race heading westward

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow
in an across clue, going west means right to left, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: read right to left across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Planes in an air race fly west over a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' looks like an airfield in this surface; it is a sporting ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed ground for sport or contest, and field is a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Cut acerbic leader by journalist

indicators.note: the leader comes first, so the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: its first letter
x is the multiplication sign, read as by, as in 3 by 4
ED is short for editor, the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued editor slashes a journalist's copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like a link word; it supplies the times sign used in dimensions.
explanation.definitionFit: Axed means chopped or abolished, the past tense of cut in the sense of scrapped.

clue.text: Threats start off body searches

indicators.note: with its start taken off, the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: to frisk is to search a person's body

explanation.surface: Threats begin pat-downs at security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' looks like begin; it means remove the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Risks are dangers that might happen, and threats in the sense of possible harms match closely.

clue.text: In the end Eva Peron's accepted by revolutionary guard

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept
to be accepted by is to be taken in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: Che Guevara is the crossword revolutionary
its last letter
taken as written; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Eva Peron is finally welcomed by a revolutionary bodyguard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' looks like 'finally'; it applies only to Eva, so only her last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone accompanies a young person to protect and supervise them, so acts as a guard.
